note: Analyst reading of the news, written by the weekly agent from logged events. Not data. Replace every week.
headline: The US struck Iranian soil again for the first time since September, in small 'defensive' strikes: on Nov 2 it hit an anti-aircraft site on Qeshm Island after the IRGC fired a missile at a US fighter jet (#141, #142), and on Nov 6 it knocked out an air-defence system there (#149). Trump calls them 'minor' and says 'it's not a war'. No one was reported hurt.

Talks go on only through Qatar. Iran is reviewing a Qatari two-day 'bridge deal' (blockade eased and some funds freed, IAEA inspectors let in, then Hormuz reopens) (#150). Iran's security chief called the US reply 'not convincing' (#144) and Rubio says there is no breakthrough and Iran's demands are 'outrageous' (#157).

More pressure without big strikes: new Treasury sanctions on Nov 4 and Nov 6 (#145, #151), a US jet disabled the blockade runner M/V Huda on Nov 7 (#152), and CENTCOM set up Task Force Iron Gate to block Iran's land and Caspian routes (#153).

Threats on both sides: Trump says he will decide 'very soon' whether to 'destroy what is left' of Iran but that new strikes are 'highly unlikely' if talks progress (#148, #157); the IRGC lifted its 2,000 km missile-range limit and Araghchi warns of 'hell' if attacks resume (#155, #156).

Shipping: a tanker hit in the Gulf on Nov 5 lost one crew member (#146); UKMTO reported another tanker hit on Nov 5 and a tanker on fire off Khasab, Oman on Nov 7 (#147, #154). The IRGC claims more ships hit mines.
